Every final module compiled with warnings treated as errors. All 200 expected axiom reports were

explicit project declarations. Mathlib’s compiled cache was reused, not independently rebuilt.
The negative controls cover a false equality, a proof placeholder, the old false normalized finite-
difference bound, the false even-length extension, and a false extra digit of precision. Missing imports
and timeouts do not count as successful rejection. The placeholder is rejected by warnings-as-errors,
and sorryAx is separately excluded from the axiom audit.
Independent finite arithmetic checks
Exact Python mirrors passed 234 reconstruction rows and 2,340 truncation-depth cases for odd lengths
1 through 35 and even degrees 0 through 24. They also checked 468 coefficients of each generating-
function identity, 13 signed-zigzag bridges and seven invalid-input controls. These are rational/integer
calculations, not executions extracted from Lean. The first-block mirror suite was rerun separately. The
original historical numerical suite was not recovered or rerun.
Provenance and limits
All eight upstream proof files, the original 28-page corrected manuscript and the first supplement
are preserved. The initial clean baseline and a preliminary successful second-block build are separate
from the final build that includes the explicit matrix row-action theorem. Eight failed development
drafts and their diagnostics are retained, not counted as successful proofs. An unsupported interactive
container invocation was replaced by successful noninteractive runtime recovery. Every archive-part
hash and the combined hash matched.

Cumulative proof checks
Lean 4.34.0-rc2 rebuilt all 21 local modules into a fresh directory with warnings treated as errors. All
272 theorem declarations and 60 explicit definitions matched their expected transitive axiom reports.
Only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, or subsets thereof, occurred. All nine dependency
pins matched. Twelve invalid-proof controls were rejected.
All 74 infrastructure and release tests passed. Historical version-specific tests use immutable metadata
snapshots. Current source counts, preserved upstream hashes, exact newly covered manuscript items,
remaining items and substantive mathematical boundary cases are checked by the active suite.
Ten targeted development runs preceded the cumulative build. Six failed before repair, due to
elaboration, coercions, finite-sum normalization, an inferred index type and tactic or linter diagnostics.
Those drafts and compiler outputs remain in a separate inactive evidence directory. No failed draft is
counted as a passing theorem.
Independent exact-rational mirrors
The new standard-library Python program uses repeated difference tables and independently evaluated
binomial sums. It passed 2,079 reconstructed values, 15,939 in-range sample differences, 2,600 arbitrary-
interpolant differences, 900 weighted cases, 966 unit-mode cases and 350 finite-mode-sum cases. Among
the weighted cases, 522 differences were zero. It also rejected 189 out-of-range stencils and 15 nonunit
inputs.
These are finite tests on rational examples, not executable extraction of Lean functions, a substitute
for a universal proof, or a new run of the manuscript’s historical experiments.

from elapsed time in the fresh-extraction release audit.

Detailed compiler logs, inventories, amendments, the completed item crosswalk, and fresh-extraction
integrity evidence accompany the release. Manuscript-to-Lean correspondence is a mathematical review,
not an automatically certified semantic equivalence.

Negative controls and infrastructure
The verifier retains its earlier 20 invalid-proof controls and adds three: a false row-zero period, a false
nondivisor period, and an unjustified extra power of the modulus. Missing imports, timeouts and
compiler panics do not count as successful rejections.
The infrastructure suite contains 162 tests. New tests verify the one-item coverage transition, preser-
vation of the 31 upstream sources, the explicit conditional flatness premise, resolution of partial targets,
and continued pending status of 7.5. Historical census tests use their frozen release snapshots. Current
census assertions use the new inventory.
Independent exact finite checks
The new rational and finite-field mirrors passed 4,848 reciprocal coefficient rows, 2,592 higher-Leibniz
cases, 4,520 reciprocal prime-shift cases, 3,720 period comparisons, and 1,476 standard-window rational
rows. They also checked 1,104 rational period differences, 620 higher differences modulo p, and 586
Dwork extraction interfaces. Eleven invalid input configurations were rejected.
A further 4,096 finite tests of the remaining global bound passed. These do not prove that bound
and do not change the coverage count. All mirrors are independent Python implementations, not
execution extracted from Lean. The original historical numerical suite was not rerun.
Scope, preservation and failures
The original manuscript and all six earlier supplements remain unchanged. The new amendment re-
places the period’s dependence on the still-pending global theorem with the direct proof. Development
failures, source snapshots and logs are kept separately from the release run. A second clean build from
a freshly extracted archive is recorded in the companion release audit.
Run bashRun-Portable.sh/path/to/kit to repeat the current unit tests, cumulative finite mir-
rors and Lean verification. Run pythonscripts/check_manifest.py to check the delivered file
snapshot. The manifest does not claim that every prose sentence is equivalent to its Lean type. That
correspondence remains a mathematical review.

The negative controls preserve the earlier rejected false equalities, placeholders, invalid normaliza-
tions and unit pivots. Four new controls demand an extra power in the sharp singular example, remove
the factorial loss, misuse a composite base, or center a ratio at the wrong constant. An infrastructure
timeout or missing import is not an accepted negative result.
Independent finite checks
The standard-library Python mirror checks 328 complete residue families for primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, includ-
ing 233 higher-residue families. It checks 4,264 integral unnormalized coefficients, 22,137 normalized
and 22,137 unnormalized difference bounds, and 1,640 comparisons with a separately computed ordi-
nary reciprocal. Further checks cover 108 weighted differential iterations, 205 integer Frobenius-square
cases and 180 exact Picard agreement prefixes.
These are finite exact-arithmetic checks, not extracted Lean code and not substitutes for the universal
formal proofs. The old normalization counterexample and the new sharp exponent-two example remain
visible.
Preservation and limitations
All 57 earlier proof modules and the original 28-page status-corrected manuscript are retained un-
changed. The new supplement and amendments give the current proof route. Historical failed drafts
and interrupted recovery attempts are retained separately from accepted builds. Historical tests that
assert an older unfinished status now read that frozen historical status. Current tests require the actual
unconditional capstone theorem before accepting completion.
The portable Lean and Mathlib versions are pinned. Mathlib’s compiled dependency cache is reused,
not independently rebuilt. The historical numerical experiment suite and Papers I–VIII are not rerun.
The two native conjectures remain unproved. No independent historical-priority assessment is made.
Manuscript-to-Lean correspondence remains mathematical review, not a theorem equating natural-
language prose with formal types.

exact object and runs #print axioms for every public named declaration selected by its inventory. Only
propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are allowed in the transitive audit. It finally tests three

15 Package contents, Markdown files and rebuilding this document
Complete production source is in formal_release/lean/. It includes all reused dependencies. The
directory also supplies the registered manifest, replay scripts, consumers, invalid controls, preserved
compiler/axiom logs, inherited verification records, preservation ledgers and required predecessor in-
ventory records. The original raw production sources are unchanged. The native contract consumers
and their separate provenance are in native_contract_evidence/.
The data/ folder supplies JSON and CSV forms of the complete source catalog, declaration census,
direct import audit and revised 49-claim crosswalk. Every catalog record includes its full source hash.
SOURCE_SHA256SUMS.txt hashes all production sources. excerpts/ contains 24 full exact core modules,
their documented typography copies, and the excerpt index with source hashes. These exact files allow
every excerpt’s ambient hypotheses and proof text to be inspected without relying on the PDF.
Markdown (.md) files are included. README.md explains the guide package, evidence scope and build
commands. SCOPE_AND_AUDIT.md explains counts, assumptions and final self-review. Preserved release
Markdown notes describe the September replay, final two claims, historical failures and mathematical
self-review. Markdown is plain text and can be read without TeX or Lean.
From the release root, build this guide together with the other readers using Python 3.10 or later,
TeX Live with XeLaTeX, fontspec, unicode-math, fvextra, microtype, booktabs, longtable, fancyhdr
and hyperref, and Poppler’s pdfinfo, pdftotext, pdffonts. Install P052, Nimbus Sans, DejaVu Sans
Mono, and Latin Modern Math as local build dependencies. Standalone font files are not distributed.
